sentences.text: Zhuchengtyrannus was a massive meat-eating theropod reaching roughly 10 meters in length and weighing about 5 metric tons.
Scientists David W. E. Hone and colleagues first named this animal in 2011.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — came from the Zangjiazhuang quarry in Zhucheng City and dates to at least 73.5 million years ago.
The quarry where the fossil was found was a Cretaceous floodplain known for having an exceptionally high number of dinosaur remains.
Other creatures sharing this site included Sinoceratops, hadrosaurs, Shantungosaurus, and various ankylosaurs.
This animal belongs to the group Tyrannosaurini within the family Tyrannosauridae.
A 2013 study identified Zhuchengtyrannus as the closest relative to Tarbosaurus.
Later research in 2024 confirmed that Zhuchengtyrannus is the nearest living relative of Tarbosaurus.
Zhuchengtyrannus lived during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in Shandong Province, China.
Experts debate whether isolated teeth from the 1970s named Tyrannosaurus zhuchengensis actually belong to Zhuchengtyrannus or a different species.
